subject: Maths
title: Long multiplication
subtitle: Multiplication and Division (Multi-Digit) · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can multiply 2- and 3-digit numbers using the long multiplication (column) method.

key_vocab.definition: Long multiplication is the column method for multi-digit × multi-digit. We multiply by each digit separately, then add.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can multiply 2- and 3-digit numbers using the long multiplication (column) method.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Long multiplication -- Long multiplication is the column method for multi-digit × multi-digit. We multiply by each digit separately, then add.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Multiply by each digit of the bottom number separately. Each new row shifts left by one column (place value).
23 × 45 = 1035
Two rows, then add

Key examples:
  ✓ 23 × 45 = 1035  (2-digit)
  ✓ 146 × 27 = 3942  (3-by-2 digit)
  ✓ Multiply units, then tens  (two rows then add)
  ✗ Forget the placeholder 0  (answer wrong)
  ✗ Multiply only the units  (incomplete)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – 2 by 2 digit
  Calculate 23 × 45
  23 × 5 = 115 (units row)
  23 × 40 = 920 (tens row, with 0 placeholder)
  115 + 920 = 1035
  = 1035
  (Always add a placeholder 0 when multiplying by the tens digit.)

Example 2 – with carrying
  Calculate 47 × 36
  47 × 6 = 282 (units row)
  47 × 30 = 1410 (tens row)
  282 + 1410 = 1692
  = 1692
  (Show carries clearly above each column.)

sections.title: 2 by 2 digit
sections.content:
Two rows, then add. Don't forget the placeholder 0.

(a) 23 × 45
(b) 62 × 38
(c) 47 × 26
(d) 84 × 19

sections.title: Word problems
sections.content:
Set up a multiplication, solve.

(a) 27 boxes of 36 = ___
(b) School trip: 14 coaches × 52 seats = ___
(c) 8 weeks at 175 mins/week = ___
(d) 23 packs of 48 stickers = ___

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✗ 23 × 45 = 23 × 4 × 5
✓ Add a placeholder 0 when multiplying by tens
✓ 47 × 36 = 1692
✓ Multiplication is commutative: 23×45 = 45×23
✗ 304 × 25 = 760 (forget last 0)
